result:
task: Round 2 of W2-54 (DAEO-0rfi, FULL): write acceptance cases for the new KPI line (the same text always gets the same query vector, stored and keyed by model, revision and exact text) before the implementation, and show them red.

status: DONE. 15 new cases are committed in `2fb42c81`; the 7 that test the new behaviour are red for the reason the README gives, and 8 are guards that pass today. One package (P-R2-1) is returned on how this line fits with "a search that may not write" (DEC-379, DEC-322).

work_completed:
- Startup checks matched: `independent-test-designer`, `DAEO-0rfi`, `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-54`, `w2/W2-54`, head `5ac58b7a`.
- Built a stand-in embedder in this suite's support file (`EmbedderStandIn`), on a loopback port at `OLLAMA_HOST`. It behaves as the owner's finding describes: a text embedded right after a different text gets `unit(own + 0.35 × previous)`; a repeat, or the very first text, gets its own vector. The size is exaggerated on purpose so the change shows in hit order and in a context's items.
- The stand-in can also send a question to one chosen file's words, matched character for character on the end of the text sent ("targets"). It can report another digest in its model list, fail with HTTP 500, or return one vector fewer than asked. It records every request.
- New file `test_w2_54_query_vector.py`: 11 functions, 15 cases. Every case goes through public interfaces only: `semantic.search(root, q, refresh=False)` (hits, order, distance), `retrieve.retrieve`, `gov context --json`, and the context check run as declared. No case says where or how a vector is kept.
- The fixtures are temporary repositories built from scratch, each with its own store. The context fixture has three tickets with different titles.
- The README has a new "Round 2" section: the line mapped to its cases, the red reason per case, the stand-in, the real-embedder case, run times, the tension, and the risks. No round-1 case was changed, so there is no `Rewrite-Reason`.
- KPI parts and their cases:
  - **Part 1 (one text, one vector, whatever came before):**
    - `…same_answer_across_processes` (red)
    - `…same_answer_within_one_process` (red)
    - `test_the_retrieval_s_public_entry_gives_one_bundle…` (red)
    - `test_with_the_real_embedder_one_question_gives_one_answer…` (red here)
  - **Part 2 (two computations of every ticket's context give one hash):**
    - `test_gov_context_twice_for_each_ticket_with_others_between_gives_one_packet` (red)
    - `test_the_context_check_is_green_over_several_tickets…` (red)
  - **Part 3 (a stored vector is never used for another key):**
    - `test_a_stored_vector_is_not_used_under_another_revision_and_is_used_again_when_the_revision_matches` (red on its last part)
    - `test_a_text_that_differs_in_any_character_gets_its_own_answer[case, spacing, trailing-newline, unicode-normal-form]` (pass)
  - **Part 4 (the first answer is the embedder's vector):** `test_a_question_asked_for_the_first_time_gets_the_vector_the_embedder_returns_for_it` (pass)
  - **Part 5 (a failed or partial call leaves nothing behind):** `test_a_failed_embedding_gives_no_hit_and_leaves_nothing_a_later_search_uses[fail, short]` (pass)
  - **Part 6 (two projects never share vectors):** `test_two_projects_do_not_share_query_vectors` (pass; it also checks that nothing is written in the other project's runtime folder or under `HOME`)
- The model part of the key: no public interface selects another model (that is W2-32's "swap by configuration"). The README says so. The revision case holds it instead: another build of the model is another key, and every embedding request must name the pinned `qwen3-embedding:0.6b`.

tests:
- `test_w2_54_query_vector.py`: 7 failed, 8 passed in 61 s on the first run, which included Ollama loading the model; 22 s on a later run.
- The rest of the suite without green-here: 46 passed in 40 s.
- `test_w2_54_green_here.py` alone: 4 passed in 252 s. This result means nothing yet; see discoveries.
- Every run used the project's test command, run to its end.

discoveries:
- **Stale store:** the "green here" cases pass trivially whenever the store is stale. My uncommitted test files made this worktree's indexes stale. `retrieve(DAEO-0rfi)` then reports lexical and semantic both `stale` and returns 0 items. So `test_the_check_run_as_declared_on_this_repository_ends_green_within_its_limit` passed in 31 s and `test_gov_check_gives_context_reproducibility_green_here` passed, though round 1 saw 14 tickets red on a fresh store. Any commit after the lead's rebuild, including mine, does this.
- **Context question:** as seen at the stand-in, a ticket's context sends the embedder only the first word of the ticket's title (`Sourdough`, `Harbour`, `Pear`). With titles that all began with "the", every context sent `the` and the check was green. This is outside this round; it may be worth a row.
- **Revision at search time:** today a search with `refresh=False` asks the embedder `/api/version` and `/api/embed`, never `/api/tags`. The revision case therefore needs the implementation to read the revision when it searches.

risks:
- The stand-in's variation is larger than the real one (0.35 against at most 0.002 per component). The cases depend only on its shape: different after another text, stable on a repeat. The real-embedder case holds the real size.
- The revision case reads "keyed by the model's revision" strictly: it means the revision the model list reports now, not the one the index was built with. An implementation that keys by the index's revision fails it. Under another revision the case accepts either the new build's answer or the facet unavailable with no hit (CAP-19 is undecided).
- "The same answer" means equal float distances, so a vector kept at lower precision than the first search used would fail.
- The real-embedder case starts this machine's Ollama if it is not running, and leaves it running (DEC-261). It ran here.

lessons:
- Run the green-here cases and the run-as-declared case only after a full rebuild at the commit under test, and read `gov check`'s index-freshness beside them.
- A context fixture needs tickets whose titles begin with different words, or the variation never shows.

proposed_decisions:
- **P-R2-1 — how the new line fits with "a search that may not write"**
  - **Question:** may a search with `refresh=False`, run by any role, store a query vector?
  - **Why now:** DEC-379 says "`refresh=False` never writes", and W1-19's interface table says the same. DEC-322 says only orchestrator-role sessions write the live store. The retrieval entry, and so `gov context` and the context check, search with `refresh=False`. My cases require the same answer across separate processes, with no `GOV_ROLE`.
  - **Which W1-19 case is at risk:** none has to turn red. `test_a_search_that_may_not_write_reports_a_missing_index_and_writes_nothing` asks a project with no index, so it stays green if a vector is stored only where an index exists. The decided texts do conflict.
  - **Options:**
    - (a) Re-baseline narrowly: a stored query vector is derived cache, kept per project apart from the index and record graph, and may be written by any search. DEC-379's "never writes" is read as "never writes the index or the record graph", and W1-19's README line is amended by its owner. Cost: one owner entry and one line of W1-19's README. Fully reversible.
    - (b) Only writer sessions store vectors; other searches use a stored vector if one exists, else embed and keep it in memory only. This keeps DEC-322 literal, but `gov context` in worker sessions stays unstable across processes, and my cross-process cases fail. Cost: the KPI is only partly met.
    - (c) Defer: no cost now, but the line is not met.
  - **Recommendation:** (a). **Confidence:** medium.

unresolved:
- P-R2-1 is open.
- The real meaning of the green-here cases waits for a rebuild at the engineer's final commit.
- The embedder-setting measurement (thread count, seed) is the engineer's to record; no case judges it.

recommended_next_action: The lead takes P-R2-1 to the owner, starts the engineer on `2fb42c81` with the 7 red cases as targets, and rebuilds the store at the engineer's final commit before running the green-here and run-as-declared cases.
